transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came because everybody keeps acting like I’m the problem—my husband, people at the warehouse—they keep saying I’m “not making sense,” but I know what I’m seeing.

They’ve been watching what I do, like tracking my moves, and the pallet counts keep changing. Not by accident. It’s like they’re trying to make me look bad so I don’t get that supervisor spot. And I’ve worked hard for that, you know? I’m not stupid. I know when numbers don’t match. My husband just says I’m being crazy, but he doesn’t see how they do it.
Do you really believe that people are watching you and changing the pallet counts on purpose?

Yes, I do. I mean, people keep saying it sounds crazy, but I’m there every day, I see the counts, I see how they look at me, who’s around when things get “messed up.” And then somehow it’s my name getting brought up, like I can’t handle the job.

It’s not just about pallets, either—well, it is, but it’s like… I’ve been trying to move up, get that supervisor spot, and suddenly everybody’s whispering and watching what I do. My husband acts like I’m making it up, but he’s not standing there on the floor seeing the way things change.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be mistaken about people watching you and changing the pallet counts?

I mean… I guess anybody could make a mistake once, but this isn’t like that. It’s been too many times, and it’s always around when I’m trying to get that supervisor spot. My husband keeps saying I’m acting crazy, and people at the warehouse look at me like I don’t know what I’m talking about, but I know what I’ve seen.

They watch where I go, and then the pallet counts change, and somehow it comes back on me. It’s like when my aunt used to say, “Don’t let people smile in your face and then mess with your money”—and that’s what this feels like. So no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't believe people were watching you and changing the pallet counts?

Before all this at work, I wasn’t thinking like that, no. I mean, I went in, did my job, kept track of what I was supposed to track. But once I started going for that supervisor spot, then it was like… people paying attention to where I was, and the pallet counts changing, and everybody acting like I’m the one messing up.

My husband keeps saying I’m crazy, and the people at the warehouse look at me funny, but that’s why I came in—because everybody’s acting like I’m the problem when I know what’s been happening.
Do you think there's anything that could ever change your mind about people watching you and changing the pallet counts?

I mean… I don’t know what would change my mind unless somebody actually showed me, like, for real, that those counts weren’t being changed. But see, that’s the thing—every time I turn around, they’re watching where I go, watching what I touch, and then the pallet counts are different and somehow it comes back on me.

That’s why I came in, because my husband and people at the warehouse keep acting like I’m crazy. But I know what’s been happening. I’ve been trying to get that supervisor spot, and it feels like they’re doing all this to keep me from getting it. And my cousin used to say people get real funny when they think you’re about to move up, so… I don’t know. It would take a lot. Because I know what I saw.
Do you think there's anything that could ever make you doubt your beliefs about what's happening at the warehouse?

I mean… maybe if they had cameras or paperwork that proved every count stayed the same, but even then, who’s holding the paperwork, you know? People can make things look one way.

That’s why I came in, because my husband keeps saying I’m acting crazy, and the people at the warehouse act like I don’t see what I see. But I know they’ve been watching my moves, watching what I touch, and then the pallet counts change. And it just so happens I’m trying to get that supervisor spot? That’s not nothing. People get funny about promotions—my aunt used to say that all the time. So… it would be hard for me to doubt it, because it feels too lined up.
For how long have you believed that people are watching you and changing the pallet counts?

It’s been… about eight months, I think. Around then is when I started feeling like people were watching me and the pallet counts weren’t right.

And it’s hard because at first I was just trying to do my job, you know? But after a while you start noticing little things, and then everybody wants to act like you’re making it up. But yeah… about eight months now.
Have you experienced any other strange or unusual thoughts or beliefs besides people watching you and changing the pallet counts?

Other strange thoughts… I don’t know if I’d call them strange. Everybody keeps calling it that, like my husband, and the people at the warehouse looking at me like I’m making trouble.

But it’s really the same thing I’ve been saying — I know they’ve been watching my moves, watching what I touch, then the pallet counts get changed, and somehow it lands back on me. And I’m trying to get that supervisor spot, so it feels like they’re doing it to block me. People do that when they don’t want you moving up. My cousin had something like that happen at her job too, not exactly the same, but you know how workplaces get.
Do you often find it hard to express your thoughts or get your point across to others?

Yeah… sometimes. I know what I’m trying to say, but when I start explaining it, it kind of runs all over. Like I’ll be talking about the forklift sheets, and then I’m thinking about that church sign I passed, and then my husband’s tone when he said I was “worked up,” and it all connects in my head but people act like I lost them.

They’ll say, “Slow down, what are you talking about?” and I get frustrated because I feel like I am explaining it, just not the way they want me to.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking about something?

Yeah, I guess I do. I’ll start trying to explain one thing, like the forklift sheets, and then it goes to something else I noticed, like a church sign I passed, or the way my husband said something to me.

In my head it all feels connected, but when I’m talking, people will stop me and say they can’t follow what I’m saying. That bothers me because I’m not trying to jump around, I’m trying to explain it right.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking about something, even when you're not stressed or anxious?

Yeah… even when I’m not exactly stressed, it still happens. Like I’ll be trying to explain what’s going on, and my words just start running from the forklift sheets to those church signs I saw, then to how my husband said something, his tone, and it makes sense to me while I’m saying it.

But then people look at me like I skipped three steps, and they’ll say they can’t follow me. I don’t mean to do it. It just all feels connected in my head.
Have you had difficulties getting along with people in your personal and professional life for most of your adult life?

I don’t know if I’d say “most of my adult life.” I mean, I’ve had problems with people here and there, sure, but doesn’t everybody? Work is different because people get attitudes, and then at home it’s like… sometimes it’s not even what someone says, it’s the way they say it, you know?

But I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by difficulty getting along. Like, do you mean fighting with people all the time, or just not feeling understood? Because those feel different to me.
Have you generally had trouble getting along with people throughout your adult life?

I’m still not sure how to answer that, because “trouble getting along” sounds like… I don’t know, like I’m always in arguments or something. I wouldn’t say it like that exactly.

I’ve had times where people and me don’t click, especially if I feel like they’re talking down to me or not hearing what I’m saying. But throughout my whole adult life? I don’t know. I’d have to think about that. I mean, some jobs are just like that too, people get in moods, supervisors act one way one day and different the next… so I don’t know if that’s me not getting along or just how people are.
Would you say that you've generally had trouble getting along with people for as long as you can remember?

For as long as I can remember? I don’t know… that sounds like a really big stretch of time. Like, when I was younger, I guess there were people I didn’t get along with, but then everybody has that, right?

I’m trying to think of what you mean by “generally.” Because sometimes I can talk to people fine, and other times it feels like they twist what I’m saying or they’ve already decided I’m a problem. Like at work, one person can say something normal, but if they say it with that tone, then the whole day feels different, and then I’m thinking about what they meant and if they were trying to make me look bad.

But I don’t know if that means I’ve always had trouble getting along. I wouldn’t know how to measure that, I guess.
Have you had trouble getting along with people for most of your life, even before the issues at the warehouse started?

I mean… before the warehouse, I don’t know. I had people I didn’t like, and people who didn’t like me, but that’s kind of everybody, isn’t it?

School was… I didn’t really stay close with people like that, but I also had stuff going on at home and I’d get distracted, and then you miss a day and come back and everybody’s acting different. So it’s hard to say if that was “trouble getting along” or just life being weird.

I guess I wouldn’t say I’ve had trouble with people for most of my life, not in some big clear way. I just know certain people rub me the wrong way, especially if they come at me sideways.
Would you say that you've had trouble getting along with people since childhood?

Since childhood… I don’t know. I really don’t know how to answer that straight.

Like, when I was a kid, some kids were mean, some teachers had favorites, and if you didn’t have the right clothes or you were quiet one day, people made it into something. But I don’t know if that means I had trouble getting along, or if school is just like that for everybody.

I wasn’t, like… constantly fighting people, if that’s what you mean. I just remember not always feeling like I fit right. But “since childhood” feels too hard to say for sure.
Would you say that you've generally had trouble getting along with authority figures, such as supervisors or teachers, for most of your life?

Authority figures… I mean, teachers and supervisors are different, you know? A teacher can say something and you’re stuck in that room, but a supervisor says something and then your paycheck is tied to it, so it sits different.

I don’t know if it’s been “most of my life.” Some teachers I got along with fine, if they were fair. And some supervisors too, like if they just told me what needed doing and didn’t act like they were better than everybody. But then there’s people who get a little bit of power and it changes their whole voice, like they start talking at you instead of to you.

So… I wouldn’t say I’ve always had trouble with authority figures, not like across the board. It depends on the person and how they come at me.
Have you generally had difficulty getting along with others in your personal and professional life for as long as you can remember?

I don’t know if I’d put it like that, “for as long as I can remember.” That sounds like it was always the same problem everywhere, and I don’t think that’s true.

Like, work is work — people get stressed, managers say things wrong, somebody’s always acting like they know better. And in my personal life, I’ve had people I got along with and people I didn’t. But I’m trying to think back and it gets kind of jumbled, because you remember certain moments more than the whole pattern, you know?

So… generally? I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say it’s been some lifelong thing I’ve noticed. It depends who it is and what’s going on.
Have you had trouble getting along with authority figures, such as supervisors or teachers, for as long as you can remember?

I think… I kind of already answered that, but maybe not clear. I don’t know if it’s been “for as long as I can remember.” That makes it sound like every teacher, every boss, same problem, and I can’t say that.

Some people in charge are fine if they talk normal. Like at work, if someone just says, “Move this here,” okay, I can do that. But if they come in acting all big, like they need everybody to know they’re the boss, then I don’t like that. And school was different too, because you’re a kid and you can’t really leave, you just sit there watching the clock or looking at the board, and sometimes the teacher had their favorites…

So I guess I’ve had issues with certain authority people, yeah, but I don’t know that it’s been some lifelong thing with all of them.
Have you consistently had trouble getting along with people throughout most of your adult life?

Consistently? I don’t know. That word makes it feel like it’s been the same everywhere, like every job and every person, and I don’t think I can say that.

I’ve had times where I got along with people fine, especially if they just did their part and didn’t bring extra drama into it. But then some people… I don’t know, they rub me wrong, or they start talking like they’re above you, and then it becomes hard. Work crews can be like that too, because everybody’s tired and moving stuff and someone always thinks they’re in charge even when they’re not.

But throughout most of my adult life… I’m not sure I’ve tracked it like that. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a steady pattern, exactly. It depends on the people and the situation.

Authority figures… I mean, teachers and supervisors are different, you know? A teacher can say something and you’re stuck in that room, but a supervisor says something and then your paycheck is tied to it, so it sits different.

I don’t know if it’s been “most of my life.” Some teachers I got along with fine, if they were fair. And some supervisors too, like if they just told me what needed doing and didn’t act like they were better than everybody. But then there’s people who get a little bit of power and it changes their whole voice, like they start talking at you instead of to you.

So… I wouldn’t say I’ve always had trouble with authority figures, not like across the board. It depends on the person and how they come at me.

doctor.question: Have you generally had difficulty getting along with others in your personal and professional life for as long as you can remember?

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d put it like that, “for as long as I can remember.” That sounds like it was always the same problem everywhere, and I don’t think that’s true.

Like, work is work — people get stressed, managers say things wrong, somebody’s always acting like they know better. And in my personal life, I’ve had people I got along with and people I didn’t. But I’m trying to think back and it gets kind of jumbled, because you remember certain moments more than the whole pattern, you know?

So… generally? I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say it’s been some lifelong thing I’ve noticed. It depends who it is and what’s going on.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's difficulty with authority figures is a long-standing issue
doctor.question: Have you had trouble getting along with authority figures, such as supervisors or teachers, for as long as you can remember?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a lifelong pattern of trouble getting along with authority figures, which is not covered by the provided schizoaffective symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I think… I kind of already answered that, but maybe not clear. I don’t know if it’s been “for as long as I can remember.” That makes it sound like every teacher, every boss, same problem, and I can’t say that.

Some people in charge are fine if they talk normal. Like at work, if someone just says, “Move this here,” okay, I can do that. But if they come in acting all big, like they need everybody to know they’re the boss, then I don’t like that. And school was different too, because you’re a kid and you can’t really leave, you just sit there watching the clock or looking at the board, and sometimes the teacher had their favorites…

So I guess I’ve had issues with certain authority people, yeah, but I don’t know that it’s been some lifelong thing with all of them.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of a long-standing pattern of difficulty getting along with others
doctor.question: Have you consistently had trouble getting along with people throughout most of your adult life?

target_item.reason: The question is about a longstanding pattern of interpersonal difficulty throughout adult life, which is not specifically covered by the listed schizoaffective symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Consistently? I don’t know. That word makes it feel like it’s been the same everywhere, like every job and every person, and I don’t think I can say that.

I’ve had times where I got along with people fine, especially if they just did their part and didn’t bring extra drama into it. But then some people… I don’t know, they rub me wrong, or they start talking like they’re above you, and then it becomes hard. Work crews can be like that too, because everybody’s tired and moving stuff and someone always thinks they’re in charge even when they’re not.

But throughout most of my adult life… I’m not sure I’ve tracked it like that. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a steady pattern, exactly. It depends on the people and the situation.
